# Tool reference (agent API and MCP)

The same 33 tools are available through `pcbtestkit api <tool> --args '<json>' --compact`, the MCP server (`pcbtestkit mcp`) and Python (`pcbtestkit.agent.Workspace.call`). Every call returns one JSON object with `"ok": true|false`; errors carry `code`, `message` and often `hint` or `did_you_mean`.

R = read-only, W = write (stored in `pcbtestkit.json` with an audit entry; `undo_last` reverts up to 20 writes). Every write accepts `rationale` (one sentence), `dry_run` (preview the effects) and `confirm` (needed after a `CONFIRM_REQUIRED` answer). Core = included in the MCP `core` profile (tool profiles: full, core, readonly).

| Tool | R/W | Core | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`open_project`](#open_project) | R | yes | Open a KiCad project (.kicad_pcb, .kicad_pro or folder) |

### open_project

Open a KiCad project (.kicad_pcb, .kicad_pro or folder). Needed once per session unless the server was started with --project.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` (required) | string |  |

### get_agent_guide

Short workflow and rules for using these tools. Call first if unsure.

No arguments.

### get_overview

Compact board summary: size, layers, counts, rails with expected voltages, supply, readiness, coverage, open decisions.

No arguments.

### get_open_decisions

What still needs engineering judgement, highest priority first. Each item has evidence, a suggestion and example_args for the tool named in apply_with.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `topic` | string | Only this topic (e.g. rail_voltage). |

### list_nets

List nets as compact rows [name, kind, nominal_v, min_v, max_v, pads, probe, channel].

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | Max rows (default 50, max 500). |
| `offset` | integer | Rows to skip (from next_offset). |
| `kind` | power \| ground \| signal \| unconnected \| any |  |
| `query` | string | Substring or glob (e.g. '*SDA*'). |
| `probed` | boolean | true = only nets with a probe, false = only without. |

| `max_pins` | integer |  |

### set_net_specs

Set expected voltage limits / kind / test inclusion for one or more nets (batch up to 200). Limits: nominal_v+tolerance_pct, or explicit min_v/max_v.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `updates` (required) | array of object |  |
| `updates[].net` (required) | string |  |
| `updates[].kind` | power \| ground \| signal |  |
| `updates[].nominal_v` | number \| string | Volts; number or text like '3V3', '3.3V', '1800mV'. |
| `updates[].tolerance_pct` | number | Symmetric band around nominal (0.1-50). |
| `updates[].min_v` | number \| string | Volts; number or text like '3V3', '3.3V', '1800mV'. |
| `updates[].max_v` | number \| string | Volts; number or text like '3V3', '3.3V', '1800mV'. |
| `updates[].max_current_a` | number | Design current; turns track-width checks into hard checks. |
| `updates[].test` | boolean | false = do not probe/test this net. |
| `updates[].note` | string |  |
| `updates[].clear` | boolean | Remove all decisions for this net (back to inferred values). |

| `min_idle_current_a` | number |  |

| `nest_border_mm` | number |  |

### set_batch_and_programming

Batch size (boards per fixture and jig set) and programming: headers, fixture connector type, flash command.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `batch_count` | integer | Boards per batch: one fixture site per board, jigs that hold them. |
| `batch_cols` | integer | Columns of boards (0 = automatic). |
| `bed_mm` | array of number | 3D-printer bed [x, y] mm for the jigs. |
| `program_headers` | array of string | Programming headers the fixture serves (refs); omit = auto-detected, [] = none. |
| `program_connector` | same \| swd10 \| jtag20 \| avr_isp6 \| pic_icsp6 \| pins | Fixture connector per board: same = copy of the board's header. |
| `program_command` | array of string | argv the runner uses to flash each board ({site}, {serial} filled in). |

### set_stacked_boards

Declare boards stacked on this one (daughter board, shield, display): parts, outline, height, fitted during the test or after. Replaces the whole list; [] clears it.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `boards` (required) | array of object |  |
| `boards[].name` | string |  |
| `boards[].refs` | array of string | Connectors it plugs into, or the footprint that draws the stacked board. |
| `boards[].side` | top \| bottom |  |
| `boards[].outline` | array of number | [x0, y0, x1, y1]: its shadow on this board, KiCad board coordinates in mm. Default: outline of refs (an estimate for connectors). |
| `boards[].height_mm` | number | Top of the stack above this board's surface. |
| `boards[].fitted_at_test` | boolean | true (default): on the board during the test; false: fitted after it. |

### set_analysis_options

Analysis settings: class system + class you will order (class_system e.g. 'jlcpcb-2026', tech_class e.g. '6C' or 'standard'), extra class checks (class_checks e.g. ['ipc-2221-voltage:B2']), tech_context (finish, mask_color, edge_process, system parameters), tech_layers, base_copper_um, fab_profile, fab_overrides, thresholds, ignore_checks. list_class_systems shows the choices.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `class_system` | string \| null | Class system id; null = default (eurocircuits-2024). |
| `tech_class` | string \| null | Class of that system, e.g. 6C, standard, 4-layer; null clears it. |
| `class_checks` | array of string | Extra systems to check, 'system' or 'system:class'; replaces the list. |
| `tech_context` | object | Merged into tech.context; null value removes a key. e.g. {finish: 'ENIG', mask_color: 'black', registration_mm: 0.05} |
| `tech_layers` | integer \| null | Copper layer count you will order. |
| `base_copper_um` | number \| null | Outer base copper in um (12/18/35/70/105). |
| `fab_profile` | advanced \| conservative \| standard |  |
| `fab_overrides` | object | e.g. {min_track: 0.1} |
| `thresholds` | object | Keys of the 'analysis' config section, e.g. decoupling_max_mm. |
| `ignore_checks` | array of string |  |

### list_class_systems

Technology-class systems available (fab class tables, fab capability tiers, IPC standards), with their dimensions and levels. Use the id with set_analysis_options/check_classes.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | fab-classes \| fab-capability \| standard |  |

### describe_class_system

Limits of a class system: per level, or resolved for this board (resolved=true with a class).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `system` (required) | string |  |
| `class` | string | e.g. 6C; omit for all levels. |
| `resolved` | boolean | Resolve conditional rules for this board (needs class). |

### check_classes

Evaluate the board against class systems: class needed, fits or not, and the features that block. Without arguments: every system. With target: compliance with that class of one system.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `systems` | array of string |  |
| `target` | string |  |
| `max_items` | integer | Violation locations per parameter (default 3). |

### add_class_system

Add or replace a class system from a JSON definition (fab capability page, class table, standard). It is validated first (metric names, units, conditions, level order, its own test vectors) and stored in the project config (tech.systems). get_schema('class_system') gives the format, metric names and a template.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `definition` (required) | object |  |

### waive_finding

Accept a weak point on purpose (kept out of the score, listed as waived in the spec). Needs a reason.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `check_id` (required) | string | Check id like ASM-MLCC-EDGE, or a finding uid like F004. |
| `refs` | array of string | Limit to these refs (default: all). |
| `reason` (required) | string |  |

### add_test_step

Add a functional/custom test step (voltage checks on probed nets, current window, wait, operator check, GPIO, UART expect, command). Inserted before power-off. See get_schema('test_step').

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `step` (required) | object |  |

### remove_test_step

Remove a custom step by id (built-in steps S1-S9 come from the board; change options instead).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | string |  |

### add_manual_check

Add a visual/operator inspection item to step S1 (e.g. 'connector J1 latch closed').

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `check` (required) | string |  |
| `refs` | array of string |  |

### undo_last

Revert the previous write (up to 20 steps; kept across CLI calls and sessions).

No arguments besides rationale/dry_run/confirm.

### validate

Check that decisions are complete and consistent. errors must be fixed; warnings are advisory.

No arguments.

### generate_outputs

Write spec JSON, test plan, fixture .kicad_pcb (+probes CSV), solder jig STL/SCAD, HTML report and the Pi runner bundle. Returns paths and a summary, not file contents.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `out_dir` | string |  |
| `outputs` | object | {spec, testplan, fixture, jig, report, runner, guide, visuals, video: bool}; video renders a 3D-animated explainer with KiCad and takes several minutes |
| `run_kicad_checks` | boolean | Run KiCad DRC/ERC via kicad-cli (slower). |

### read_output

Read part of a generated JSON file (spec\|testplan\|fixture\|jig) via a JSON pointer, truncated to max_chars.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` (required) | spec \| testplan \| fixture \| jig |  |
| `pointer` | string | e.g. /electrical/supply or /probes/0 |

| `max_chars` | integer |  |
